observations: Small blue plastic children's keyboard toy with 5 colored piano-style keys, each printed with a cartoon dog character (Bluey).
Top right has a round button labeled 'Bluey' logo and a music-note icon.
An orange carry handle is attached to the right side.
Photo 1 shows the back of the unit with a battery compartment cover, screw, and some printed text that is too small/blurry to read clearly (appears to be a model/battery code).
No adapter, box, or power cable is visible in either photo.
No video or audio evidence of sound, lights, or button response.

claims.claim: Blue electronic piano with all Bluey songs and other songs preloaded
claims.evidence: No audio/video provided; photos show only static keys.
No demonstration clip or screen shown.
No video of keys being pressed or sound playing.
No adapter visible in either photo.
No receipt, packaging, or UK plug/voltage sticker shown.
No audio clip or video to confirm sound quality.

risks.risk: Keys or sound module may not function (dead key, no sound, crackling speaker)
risks.proof: Short video of each key being pressed with audible sound

risks.risk: Adapter claimed but not shown; could be missing or incompatible (UK plug vs Nigeria socket)
risks.proof: Photo of the actual adapter/cable included

risks.risk: Battery compartment or internal wiring condition unknown (corrosion, loose battery contacts)
risks.proof: Close-up photo of open battery compartment interior
risks.if_unproven: priced as risk of internal fault, not fully functional

risks.risk: Cosmetic wear, cracks, or sticker peeling on keys not visible from these angles
risks.proof: Additional close-up photos from multiple angles under good light
risks.if_unproven: priced as moderate wear, not mint

proof_requests: Video of the piano powered on, each key pressed, demonstrating sound and lights
Photo of the adapter/cable that is claimed to be included
Close-up photo of the battery compartment interior
Clearer photo of the model/serial text on the back panel
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a Bluey-branded children's toy keyboard, but none of the functional claims (sound, keys working, adapter) are verifiable from the photos alone, so it must be priced at worst case as a non-working or incomplete unit until proof is given.
